title: Mexico Silences Critics Again, TAKES DOWN Major Crime Boss – Soberanía 133
author: Mexico Solidarity
content:
Support the show! <https://www.gofundme.com/f/keep-soberania-on-air>

In episode 133 of Soberanía, hosts Kurt Hackbarth and José Luis Granados Ceja
cover Mexico's capture of El Chapo Isidro, Mexico's rejection of
"narcoterrorism" at the OAS, and the US pause on joint operations with
Ecuador.

![🇲🇽](https://s.w.org/images/core/emoji/17.0.2/72x72/1f1f2-1f1fd.png) Mexico
captures El Chapo Isidro—a key drug trafficker linked to the Beltrán Leyva
Cartel and the Mayo faction of the Sinaloa Cartel—in a months-long, surgical
military operation. We unpack why this matters, the troubling history of his
four previous arrests and releases under conservative governments, and the
US's attempt to steal credit for the operation.

![🌎](https://s.w.org/images/core/emoji/17.0.2/72x72/1f30e.png) Mexico stands
firm at the OAS, rejecting the term "narcoterrorism" and pushing back against
a militarized US drug strategy. Ambassador Alejandro Encinas delivers a
principled defense of Mexican sovereignty—and we explain why the Río Treaty's
"reciprocal assistance" is nothing but a cover for US interventionism.

![🇪🇨](https://s.w.org/images/core/emoji/17.0.2/72x72/1f1ea-1f1e8.png) The
Trump administration pauses joint military operations with Ecuador over
alleged human rights abuses—yes, you read that right. We discuss what this
means for Daniel Noboa's government ahead of Sunday's local elections, and why
even far-right governments in the region are getting cold feet about US
security cooperation. Plus: tune un on November 26 for our exclusive interview
with Andrés Arauz!

![📌](https://s.w.org/images/core/emoji/17.0.2/72x72/1f4cc.png) We're also
launching our annual fundraiser! If you value independent, English-language
coverage of Mexico and Latin America, please consider supporting the show.
Every donation helps us keep the lights on and reach 10,000 views per week.
